title: Severe outage quick comm kits and cribsheet
content:
Purpose:
This cribsheet is a compact, on-shift reference for rapid, clear communications during severe outages (S1/S2). It focuses on the messages we post (internal and external), the cadence for updates, and the minimum operations the on-call should complete before escalating outreach to customers or legal. Designed to sit on the war-room monitor or in the incident channel for easy copy/paste.

Scope and when to use this: 
- Use for incidents with customer-visible impact (latency spikes >30s, sustained error rates, persistent inability to serve requests, or data-plane degradation).
- Not intended for brief transient errors resolved automatically within 5 minutes.

Core roles (quick reference):
- Incident Commander (IC): owns triage, mitigation plan, and final go/no-go for external comms.
- Comms Lead: crafts external messages, coordinates with CS and Legal, posts to status and customer channels.
- Engineering Liaison: provides technical updates and ETA estimates.
- Customer Success (CS) Liaison: identifies high-risk customers and prepares targeted outreach.
- SRE Scribe: keeps timeline and action log, timestamps every update.

Initial checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Confirm impact scope (regions, models, APIs, customers) and severity level.
- Open incident ticket (JIRA) and attach short summary, impact, and initial owner.
- Create incident channel (Slack/Signal/Bridge) and invite IC, Comms Lead, Engineering Liaison, CS Liaison.
- Post first internal bridge summary (see template A).
- Decide whether to post to status page (see decision rules below).

Decision rules for status page:
- Post an initial status page entry if any of the following:
  * >1% of requests returning errors for >5 minutes,
  * single-customer critical failure (data loss, inability to API auth), or
  * multi-region outage affecting production.
- If impact is limited to internal testing or staging, do not post.
- If the impact is user-perceivable but a workaround exists (e.g., reduced throughput), post with "degraded performance" status.

Update cadence and timing guidance:
- First external/status message: within 30 minutes of confirming user-visible impact.
- Update cadence while unresolved: every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours, then hourly unless the situation changes faster.
- If the incident is escalated to execs or legal, switch to 15-minute updates until stabilized.

Templates (copy/paste friendly)
A) Internal bridge summary (first post)
Title: INCIDENT OPEN: [short impact summary] (IC: @handle)
Body:
- What: [one-line summary, e.g., "API 503s for /v1/generate in us-west-2"]
- When first observed: [HH:MM UTC]
- Impact: [broad strokes — % of requests/customers affected]
- Owner/IC: @[name]
- Next steps: [triage action being taken]
- Ask: [what you need from the channel — e.g., logs, restarts, config rollbacks]

B) Status page short (public) — initial post for degraded or outage
Headline: We are investigating an issue affecting [service / region]
Details:
- What we know: [concise bullet — e.g., "Some customers are receiving 503 errors for the text generation API in us-west-2."]
- Scope: [percent of traffic or sample services affected]
- Current status: Investigating
- Mitigation in progress: [short — e.g., "rolling back recent deploy to canary" or "increasing capacity"]
- ETA: [if available, otherwise "We will provide updates every 30 minutes."]
- Contact / affected customers: [support@redwood.ai or link to status subscription]

C) Status page update (recovery / resolved)
Headline: Service restored for [service / region]
Details:
- What happened (short): [one-line root cause or if pending RCF: "under investigation"]
- What we did: [short mitigation steps]
- Customer impact: [duration window + any data loss — if none, say "no data loss"]
- Next steps: Post-incident review scheduled and timeline for RCA

D) Targeted customer email (when specific customers are impacted)
Subject options: "Service interruption affecting API access" or "Temporary degraded performance for text-generation API"
Body (concise):
Hi [Customer name],

We’re writing to let you know about a service interruption that affected [product / API] on [date/time window UTC].

Impact: [what they may have experienced — e.g., increased latencies or 503 errors].
Scope: [approximate % of requests or list of endpoints].
Action we took: [short mitigation].
Current status: [investigating / partially mitigated / resolved].
Next update: [time or cadence].
Contact: If you require immediate assistance, contact [CS rep name] at [email/phone] or reply to this message.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

— Redwood Inference Team

E) Short internal executive update (one-liner for execs)
Time: [HH:MM UTC] — severity: [S1/S2]
Summary: [one sentence: e.g., "Text-generation API in us-west-2 experiencing 503s for ~60% of requests; mitigation rolling back canary; ETA ~45m for stabilization."]

Operational checklist (war-room actions)
- Tag owner for each mitigation step and set completion time.
- Keep timeline with timestamps (scribe).
- Collect logs and sample request IDs for CS to triage customer cases.
- If rollback is chosen, confirm safe rollback procedure and impact to in-flight requests.
- Verify alerts and thresholds are sane (silence noisy non-actionable alerts).
- Prepare post-incident comm (RCA summary draft) as soon as recovery begins.

When to involve Legal/Compliance and Executives:
- Legal: potential data exposure, regulatory impact, or contractual data breach.
- Executives: if incident is likely to be public-facing beyond customers (press, major accounts) or SLA breach with potential financial remediation.

Targeted outreach thresholds (CS rules of thumb)
- Immediate 1:1 outreach if the customer is: top-10 ARR, on Dedicated/Private infra, or explicitly flagged in the contract.
- Group email if >10 customers in a segment affected but not individually critical.

Communication do/don't list
Do:
- Be concise and timely.
- State what you know and what you don’t.
- Give a clear cadence and channel for updates.
- Offer a single point of contact for affected customers.
Don’t:
- Speculate about root cause in public posts.
- Share internal incident timelines or ticket numbers in public-facing messages (use anonymized IDs if required).

Post-incident: short-run followups
- Within 24h: post short resolved message on status page and targeted emails to flagged customers.
- Within 72h: publish RCA draft to Confluence for internal review (link to template CONFLUENCE-INC-RCA).

Examples of short phrasings (for fast copy/paste)
- "Investigating: Partial API failures affecting text generation in us-west-2. Engineers are looking into root cause. Updates every 30 minutes."
- "Mitigating: Rolling back a recent deploy to restore service; customers may see intermittent errors for the next 10–20 minutes."
- "Resolved: Service restored. We are monitoring and preparing an RCA."

Notes and reminders for on-call scribe:
- Save all messages posted to status page and incident channel in the JIRA incident ticket.
- Capture sample request ids and timestamps before rotating bridge participants.
- Keep one person responsible for CS handoffs (name and contact) in the ticket.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Incident ticket template: [JIRA-INC-8421] (attach timeline)
- Public status subscription link: https://status.redwood.ai (example)
- RCA template: CONFLUENCE-INC-RCA

End of cribsheet. Keep this doc pinned in the incident channel and update with any company-level policy changes.
